name: What does turnkey mean in luxury custom home building?

mainEntity.name: When a builder says turnkey, what is usually included and what is not?
mainEntity.text: When a builder says turnkey, what is usually included and what is not?

acceptedAnswer.text: Turnkey is a useful term, but it is not standardized. In a luxury custom home, it often means the project is completed to the point where the owner can move in, but the exact inclusions depend entirely on the contract. Some turnkey packages include site work, finishes, appliances, and basic landscaping, while others stop at the finished structure and leave furnishing, drapery, and certain outdoor elements to the owner. Because the term can be interpreted differently, homeowners should ask for a precise inclusion list rather than relying on the label. The best contract will spell out what is and is not part of turnkey delivery so there are no surprises at the end of the project.
acceptedAnswer.description: Turnkey usually means the home is delivered ready for move-in, but the exact scope varies by contract. It may still exclude furnishings, window treatments, landscaping details, or specialty systems unless they are specifically listed.
